title: Quantitative Characterization of Liquid Photosensitive Bioink Properties for Continuous Digital Light Processing Based Printing
protocol: Define three parameters: liquid absorbance (Al), solid absorbance (As), and threshold time (tT).
Rewrite the traditional Jacobs working curve using these three parameters according to Equation 1.
Measure the threshold time of the bioink using a rheometer equipped with an element for temperature control.
Use a 365 nm light source to expose the testing platform of the rheometer.
Set the rheometer to get the Time-Moduli data during a period of 300 s, taking each data point every 0.3 s through the Time Settings options in the rheometer software.
Click the Start Test button of the rheometer and simultaneously click the Start Button of the light source.
Count from the start of exposure; when the storage modulus data equals the loss modulus data, recognize the corresponding time as the threshold time.
Record manually the threshold time.
Build the absorbance test equipment using two upper and lower glass slides to clamp a ring-shaped printed structure.
Place the clamped ring on the test area of the light intensity meter.
Measure the incident light intensity (Ii) when the test chamber is empty.
Fill the test chamber with 10 µL of bioink.
Expose the test chamber containing bioink to UV light at 365 nm.
Obtain the light intensity (Ilh) from the absorbance test equipment after exposure.
Obtain the light intensity (Ish) when the bioink is fully cured and the value no longer changes.
Obtain the Jacobs working curve according to the obtained parameters.
Set the exposure time of the first single layer as the threshold time (tT) in the DLP software's parameter settings.
Calculate the exposure time for curing 10 µm thick materials using Equation 1.
Subtract the threshold time from the calculated exposure time to obtain the real exposure time for a single layer.
Set the time interval between adjacent layers to 0 s in the DLP software's parameter settings.
Start the printer by clicking the Start button in the printing software.
Finish printing by clicking the Stop button in the printing software when the process ends.
